name: The Guesthouse Hotel
welcomeMessage: Curated by our team — the spots we actually send friends to.

recs.name: Hopleaf Bar
recs.shortDescription: Belgian beer and the mussels everyone in the neighborhood argues about.
recs.staffNote: Ask for a table in the back room if it's busy up front.

recs.name: Marty's Martini Bar
recs.shortDescription: A tiny, cash-only bar with the best martini in the neighborhood — no TVs, no phones at the bar.
recs.staffNote: Get there before 9pm on weekends, it fills up fast.

recs.name: Kopi, A Traveler's Cafe
recs.shortDescription: Global tea and coffee spot with floor cushions and a genuinely great chai.

recs.name: Women & Children First
recs.shortDescription: Legendary feminist bookstore with an incredible staff-picks wall.

recs.name: Big Jones
recs.shortDescription: Southern comfort food done seriously — the fried chicken and biscuits are worth the wait.
recs.staffNote: Weekend brunch reservations go fast, book ahead.

recs.name: M.Henry
recs.shortDescription: A brunch institution — think French toast the size of your head, kid-friendly and unpretentious.

recs.name: Middle Eastern Bakery & Grocery
recs.shortDescription: Fresh pita, olives, and spices — pick up a picnic here before heading to the lake.

recs.name: Simon's Tavern
recs.shortDescription: Dive bar with a nautical theme and a glögg (Swedish mulled wine) worth the trip alone.

recs.name: Andersonville Galleria
recs.shortDescription: A co-op of over 100 local artists and makers, tucked behind an unassuming storefront.

recs.name: Hamburger Mary's
recs.shortDescription: Burgers, drag brunch, and a party atmosphere — Andersonville's loudest good time.
